get.summary:
The health of the daemon: what it runs, what it keeps its
records in, where it reaches Docker, and how much work waits.
Every machine of every Person, with whether it is connected.
get.description:
It sits beside the Sessions, because a host action needs a present
client and not only a Session: an administrator who reads that nobody
can run a host command reads it here.

post.summary: Create an account and the person's Workspace.
post.description:
The Workspace comes from the same seed a local first run uses, so the
person signs in to a sprite that can already think: the Org's
provider keys serve them and they hold none of their own.

post.summary:
Disable an account. Every Session of the person goes with it, so a
client that holds one stops working at once rather than at its
expiry. The Workspace and everything in it stay, so re-enabling gives
the same person the same records back.

Reset a password. Every Session of the person ends with it: a
password reset that left a stolen Session alive would reset nothing.

put.summary: Give a Person the address and the password they sign in with.
put.description:
The seeded Person of a local installation holds neither: the
Client App trades the Client Credential for a Session, so nothing
asks them for a password until they want a browser to sign in without
the client. This is where they set one.

Both halves are written at once, because an address without a
password and a password without an address are each half a way in.
The Sessions of the Person end with it, as a reset does, unless the
Person is the Administrator who asks: signing yourself out of the
interface you are using tells nobody anything.

get.summary:
Every provider the installation sets up, with where each part
stands.

put.summary:
Set up one part. A Connection part that exists takes a new secret
and proves it again; its other fields stay, and removing the part is
how they change.

delete.summary:
Remove one part. A carrier that carries a number and a mail domain
that holds a mailbox stay, and the refusal says what to do first.
Removing the OAuth client leaves every brokered Google connection
unable to refresh, so each person consents again against the next
client (ADR-0012).

post.summary:
Prove one part's kept credential at the provider again. A key the
provider refuses leaves the Connection `reauth_required` or
`unavailable`, and the answer says why.

get.summary: What each Person's Computers take of the host.
Who is signed in, from which kind of client, and since when.

Spend per person for a period. This is the read that answers
the first billing question, and it is the Administrator's alone.

post.summary:
Put the agent's computer to sleep now, ahead of the idle
sweep. The disk survives, so the next wake finds the same data.

409.description: The computer is running a command
The local image version mismatches the pin

post.summary:
Make the Agent's mailbox. The answer arrives once the host has made
it; the login is proven afterwards, so the mailbox lands
`provisioning` and reaches `active` or `unavailable` on its own
(ADR-0019).

delete.summary:
Delete the mailbox. The user types the address to confirm it,
because the host's mail goes with the mailbox and Pagis keeps no
copy of a message body (ADR-0019).

post.summary:
Give the mailbox a new password and prove the login again. The
cursor does not move, so nothing the mailbox received while it was
unavailable is lost.

Hand the computer back to the agent: the parked run resumes
with the "screen may have changed" note. A handback without a
takeover is a no-op.

200.description: PNG bytes; a live frame when awake, the last screenshot when asleep

post.summary:
Take over the agent's computer: the daemon flips the input
switch to the user and denies the agent's screen leases.

200.description: The artifact bytes. A passive image, audio, video or plain-text type shows inline; every other type is an `application/octet-stream` attachment.

get.summary:
List the Call records of the Workspace, newest first. Home
reads it to find the calls that came in today and were missed.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: The Call the page starts after

get.summary:
Read one Call record. The strip, the call inspector and the settled
block all read this: the record is the one source of truth, and the
`call.transcript` events only add the lines that arrive after the
read.

post.summary:
Control of a live call is reserved (ADR-0020). Two-way barge-in is
not built, so it answers 501.

501.description: Control of a live call is not implemented

post.summary:
The user ends a live call. The daemon hangs up its own leg, and the
call settles with a reason like every other call (ADR-0020). The hub
is found under the Person's own Workspace, so a live call of another
Workspace answers 404, as a call that is not live.

Drop one live call to Unknown. It asks for a confirmation in the
user interface, because it cannot be undone while the call runs.
The gate is found under the Person's own Workspace, so a live call of
another Workspace answers 404, as a call that is not live.

parameters.description: Exclusive ULID cursor: only messages older than this id.

parameters.description: The index of the block to speak, in the message's block array.

200.description: The spoken block as audio bytes

get.description:
Google redirects the person's browser here on the installation's own
public origin. The request carries no Session: the Session cookie is
`SameSite=Strict`, so a browser sends none on a cross-site
navigation. The route finishes only for the browser that holds the
transaction cookie of the `state`, which the start route set. The
`state` names the Connection, and the Person and the Session that
started the authorization: that Session must still be live, and the
Google account that consented must be the account of the Connection.
A redirect without the cookie spends the `state` and connects
nothing. Each answer clears the cookie.

200.description: A page that tells the person to go back to Pagis

get.summary: Send one browser to Google for a brokered authorization.
get.description:
The authorize request answers this address, and it belongs to the
Person who asked. It sits outside the session middleware because a
browser with no Session must sign in and come back, not get `401`: it
goes to the same address in the Product App, which shows the sign-in
page and then comes back here. A Session of another Person gets a
refusal. For the initiating Person, the route sets the transaction
cookie, which binds the `state` to this browser, and redirects to
Google.

A local installation with the multi-user mode off has one Person and
answers only programs of its own machine. There the route asks the
browser for no Session: the Client App opens it in the system
browser, and the owner does not sign in a second time. The callback
keeps every check.

303.description: To Google with the transaction cookie, or to the sign-in page of the Product App when the browser holds no Session

403.description: A page that says the Session belongs to another Person

410.description: A page that says no authorization waits under this state

post.summary:
The counts one filter gives over the stored pages, for the filter
editor. One rule alone in the body gives the rule editor its line.

get.summary: The signed-in person's own machines, with presence.

get.summary:
The end of the server log of one Plugin in the asking Person's own
Workspace.
get.description:
Each Workspace runs the Org's Plugin in its own Plugin Computer and
keeps its own log of the Plugin's stderr. A server can write Person
data or a bound value to stderr, so a Person never reads the log of
another Workspace (ADR-0023). A Plugin whose servers have not written
to stderr in this Workspace answers an empty text.

200.description: The end of the server log in the asking Person's Workspace
The new state and what it changed

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: One run state, or several separated by a comma

post.summary:
Wake a Schedule now, ahead of its cadence (ADR-0022). Home
asks for the Report this way. The call is idempotent while a
Wake-up waits: it returns the one that already waits.

get.summary: The ICE servers of the installation's Media Relay (ADR-0014).
get.description:
A browser reads this before it makes its offer, because ICE servers
are fixed when the peer connection is made. The `turn` relay mints
credentials for each answer, so the answer is never cached.

200.description: Signed in; the session is in an HTTP-only cookie
Signed in as the seeded person

403.description: The request did not come from this machine, or came through a proxy

404.description: This installation holds no Client Credential

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The one-time code the `pagis` binary printed

303.description: Signed in; the browser is sent to the app

403.description: The request did not come from this machine, or came through a proxy

404.description: This installation holds no Client Credential

post.summary:
Connect an account (ADR-0012). The record lands at
`disconnected` with its binding; `authorize_connection` is the step
that sends the user to Google.

get.summary:
The Provider Catalog (ADR-0012) a person picks from: every provider
a person connects on their own, with the form each one needs. An
Installation Connection is not in it.
get.description:
The Google entry follows the installation. Where the Org holds
a Web OAuth client the form asks for the account alone, because the
client is the installation's; where it holds none the form asks for
the person's own Desktop client. The entry also says whether the
browser step can ask for a sign-in, which a local installation with
the multi-user mode off never does.

post.summary: Authorize one Connection.
post.description:
A `brokered` Google Connection answers an `authorization_url` and
returns at once. The URL is the start route on the Public Origin,
which belongs to the Person who asks: the client opens it, the person
consents at Google in that browser, and the public callback route is
what makes the Connection `connected`. Every other Connection is
finished when this returns, and `authorization_url` is absent.

post.summary:
Save a login the user already has (ADR-0013). The secret is
sealed here and never leaves the daemon again.

delete.summary:
Clear the failed-attempt count of the signed-in person's Workspace,
and end its delay (ADR-0021). A correct code clears it too. The
person is the only other party who can know that the wrong codes
were not an attack, so no tool reaches this.

get.summary:
The Mailbox Providers a new Agent could take a mailbox on. The
Agent's own route answers the same for an Agent that exists.

parameters.name: agent_name
parameters.description:
The name typed in the creation form. An empty name suggests no
local part.

get.summary:
Read one local part against the Address Ledger as the user types
(ADR-0019). The answer is advice: the ledger still refuses a taken
address when the mailbox is made.

The Provider Model List of every provider that holds a key, from the
installation's cache. A list older than the refresh interval, or
fetched with an older key, is fetched again first.

put.summary:
The model step's pick: the one model the default route names. It
answers while the Workspace has not finished onboarding, and `409`
afterwards, when the Models settings change the route.

The computer step's Docker endpoint. It answers an Administrator
while their Workspace has not finished onboarding, and `409`
afterwards.

The model step's key. It answers an Administrator while their
Workspace has not finished onboarding, and `409` afterwards.

post.summary:
The model step's check of a typed key. The daemon asks the provider
for its model list with the key, and stores the key only when the
provider answers. A key that the provider refuses is not stored, and
the refusal carries the provider's own words. It answers an
Administrator while their Workspace has not finished onboarding, and
`409` afterwards.

Buy one number. The daemon writes a purchase intent first, so a
restart in the middle of the purchase reconciles instead of buying
twice (ADR-0018).

Adopt a number the account already holds. The daemon asks the
carrier whether the account has it and records it; nothing is
bought. A number the account does not hold is refused.

get.summary:
The carrier's own list, read live. A search needs the carrier
Connection at `connected`.

post.summary:
Give the number back to the carrier. The charge stops, the record
stays for the Calls that point at it, and the number never comes
back. The confirmation that names the Agent is the UI's work.

Take the line back. The Workspace keeps the number and keeps paying
for it, which is what makes this different from a release.

Prove the provider's key with one call to the provider's model list.
The list call generates nothing and costs nothing. The check passes
when the provider answers the list, whatever the list holds, and it
fails with the provider's own words when the provider refuses the
key. A passed check also refreshes the installation's Provider Model
List of that provider.

put.summary:
Turn the anonymous analytics of the installation on or off
(ADR-0026). The analytics task reads the setting at each check, so
the change needs no restart.

Turn the multi-user mode on (ADR-0024): write the Public Origin and
the Trusted Proxy, and keep the Bind Address on loopback, where the
owner's proxy or tunnel on this machine reaches the daemon. The
change takes effect on the next start.

409.description: A server, which always serves a network

delete.summary:
Turn the multi-user mode off (ADR-0024): clear the Public Origin and
the Trusted Proxy, and bind loopback. People who signed in over the
network keep their accounts and reach nothing until the mode is on
again. The change takes effect on the next start.

409.description: A server, which always serves a network

post.summary:
Make the installation's first Administrator and keep its provider
keys. It answers on the Administration Port alone. The answer signs
the new Administrator in, so the person who completed the flow goes
straight to the product.

200.description: The administrator, with a session cookie

What the signed-in person spent. A Member reads this and nothing
else of the installation's accounting.

AddCredentialRequest.description:
The user's own login, typed into settings. This is the primary
way an existing account reaches the vault; takeover login stays as
the escape hatch.

login_url.description: The sign-in address; its registrable domain must equal `domain`.

secret.description: The password. It is sealed on arrival and never read back.

totp_seed.description: An optional base32 one-time code seed.

AdministrationAddress.description: Where a browser reaches the Administration Interface (ADR-0024).

loopback.description:
True where the port binds loopback. Only the machine that runs
the daemon reaches it then, and an administrator on another
machine reaches it through an SSH tunnel to the same port.

origin.description:
The origin of the administration port, such as
`http://127.0.0.1:4401`.

AdministrationHostDto.description:
One machine of one Person, for the read that says which clients can
act. A Session says who is signed in; a Host says which machine
a host action would run on, which is the other half of the same
question.

present.description: True while the daemon holds this machine's connection.

AdoptNumberRequest.description:
Adopt a number the carrier account already holds, and give
it to an Agent when the user added it from that Agent's page.

description.description:
One line on what to ask this Agent for, read by every other
Agent in its sprite line.

email_address.description:
The address of the Agent Mailbox it holds, or `null` when it
holds none (ADR-0019). It is a read-through view of the mailbox
record: the Agent itself carries no address.

standing_brief.description:
The standing brief (ADR-0020): what an inbound call to the
Agent's desk line is for, or `null` for none.

voice.description:
The Agent Voice (ADR-0020): a catalogue name, or `null` for the
provider's default.

AgentSyncConnection.description: One connection whose sync names the Agent as responsible.

rule_count.description: The number of rules in the Reflection Filter.

AnalyticsBlockedDto.description: Why a daemon sends no analytics whatever the setting says.

AnalyticsDto.description: The anonymous analytics of the installation (ADR-0026).

oneOf.description:
Why the daemon sends nothing whatever `enabled` says, or null
when it sends while `enabled` is true.

enabled.description:
The System Setting: whether the Administrator lets the daemon
send. On by default.

AuthorizeConnectionRequest.description:
The capabilities the user grants this Connection. An empty
list authorizes the read-only profile a new Connection starts at.

api_key.description:
A replacement carrier or mail host API key. The provider proves
it before Pagis keeps it, and a Google connection ignores it.

authorization_url.description:
The address to open for a `brokered` Google Connection: the
start route on the Public Origin. A browser with a Session of the
Person who asked goes on from there to consent at Google, and the
connection reaches `connected` when Google redirects that browser
back to this installation. A local installation with the
multi-user mode off has one Person and asks the browser for no
Session. Absent for every Connection this request already
finished.

AvailableNumberDto.description:
One number the carrier offers now, with today's price. Pagis stores
no price: this is read at search time and shown, never kept.

oneOf.description:
The secret itself. It goes to the daemon's secret store and is
never read back.

BindingValueRequest.description: What one declared config field is bound to.

BuyNumberRequest.description:
Buy one number, and give it to an Agent when the user bought it from
that Agent's page.

CallDto.description:
The Call record (ADR-0020). It is the one source of truth the
strip, the call inspector and the settled block read. `outcome` and
`ended_reason` stay apart, because they answer two questions.

agent_name.description: The Agent's external display name, and the line it called from.

purpose.description: What the call is for, from the Call Brief.

recording_artifact_id.description: The stereo WAV of the call, once it settles.

tools.description: The tools the call may use, by name.

CallSummaryDto.description:
One Call in a list, without its transcript. A page of ten-minute
calls would carry megabytes of lines that no list shows, so the
lines stay in `GET /api/v1/calls/{call_id}`.

agent_name.description: The Agent's external display name, and the line it used.

purpose.description: What the call is for, from the Call Brief.

recording_artifact_id.description: The stereo WAV of the call, once it settles.

Catalogue.description: What one connection's resource offers the filter editor.

CatalogueView.description: The Signal Catalogue of one resource and the filter it starts from.

user_member.description:
True when the user is a participant. A channel two agents opened
between themselves has agents alone, and the user reads it
without writing in it (ADR-0003).

value.description: The value the decision carries back to the run.

client_name.description: The machine name of the Client App.

last_seq.description:
The event id (`seq`) of the last frame the client saw; the
daemon replays the gap when the ring buffer still covers it.

oneOf.description:
Register this client as a Host of the signed-in person. The
machine is present while this socket lives, and absent the moment
it closes. The client is the authority for all three fields: what
the machine is called, what it runs on, and what it can do.

What one dispatched command did. `id` is the id the
`dispatch` frame carried.

ClientFrame.description:
Frames the client sends. The first frame must be `auth`. It carries
no credential: the session cookie authenticated the upgrade.

CompleteOnboardingRequest.description:
The optional onboarding extras: the user's name seeds shared
memory so every agent knows what to call them.

name.description: What the agents call the person.

provider_keys.description:
Provider keys by provider id: `anthropic`, `openai`,
`openrouter`. Every one of them is the installation's, so every
person the Administrator creates later thinks on them.

timezone.description:
The IANA timezone of the browser that makes the Administrator.
It becomes the Administrator's own, as a first sign-in's does.

ComputerDiskDto.description:
What one office keeps on disk: the bytes of that
tenant's Agent volumes, which the Desk Panel says in its footer. The
figure counts the volumes of one tenant and never the server's.

bytes.description:
The bytes the Agent volumes of the signed-in person's Workspace
hold together; `null` when Docker cannot say.

oneOf.description: Unix milliseconds.

ConfigureSetupPartRequest.description:
The values of one part's fields, by field key. A secret field passes
to the provider or the secret store and is never written to the
database. The type carries no `Debug`, so none of them reaches a log
line.

filter.description: The rules that decide which Subject Pages reflect (ADR-0011).

since.description: Earliest source date to import, as Unix milliseconds. Zero imports all history.

absent_capabilities.description:
What this Connection's provider does not do, and a sibling
provider does: a carrier that carries no text lists `texting`
(ADR-0020). The card states each one.

account.description:
The external account this Connection binds to. It is not a
secret, and the card names the account the user connected.

alias.description: The name a tool call uses to pick this account.

auth_mode.description:
`byo` when the user supplies the OAuth client, `brokered` when
the installation supplies it through its Installation OAuth Client.

capabilities.description:
What this Connection gives an Agent, from the provider's catalog
entry: `mail`, `calendar`, `mailboxes` or `telephony`.
The card follows this, not the provider name.

installation.description:
True for an Installation Connection: the carrier account or the
mail domain. The Administration Interface sets it up, and the
product shows it without a way to change it.

oneOf.description:
The mail settings of a Mailbox Provider (ADR-0019), for a
`migadu` or `manual` Connection.

sip_domain.description: The registrar the carrier's lines register at.

sip_username.description:
The SIP username of a carrier Connection, once the user
entered the credential. The password is never here.

status.description:
`disconnected`, `connecting`, `connected`, `reauth_required`, or
`unavailable` once the provider refuses the key it holds.

patch.description: The unified diff between the base tree and the Fork tree.

ContributionSummaryDto.description:
One Contribution as the list shows it: the record without its
patch. The patch reads on the Contribution's own address.

name.description: What the agents call the person.

password.description:
The first password. The person changes it later; the daemon keeps
only its argon2id hash.

description.description: One line on what to ask this Agent for.

oneOf.description:
The mailbox section of the form (ADR-0019): the Agent gets its
own Agent Mailbox as it is made. Absent gives it none, and the
user may provision one later from the Agent's page.

standing_brief.description:
What an inbound call to the Agent's desk line is for; absent or
empty declares none.

voice.description:
A name from `GET /api/v1/settings/voices`; absent or empty
declares no voice.

agent_ids.description: The agent participants of the new group channel.

CreateConnectionRequest.description:
The connect flow's second step (ADR-0012): the provider, the
names this Connection carries, and the fields the provider's
catalog entry declares.

A secret field passes through to the provider or the secret store
once and is never written to the database. The type carries no
`Debug` so none of them reaches a log line.

alias.description:
The name a tool call uses to pick this account. It is unique per
workspace and uses lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, or
underscores.

fields.description:
The values of the entry's fields, by field key. A number field
is sent as its decimal text.

anchor_at.description: Explicit Unix-millisecond anchor for an interval.

interval_minutes.description: Elapsed interval in minutes. The minimum is one minute.

local_time.description: Wall-clock input in `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` form for a one-shot Schedule.

filter.description: The typed filter for this event kind.

CredentialDto.description:
One saved login as settings shows it. There is no secret
here, and no endpoint that returns one.

has_totp.description: True when the record carries a one-time code seed.

login_url.description: The one address a fill opens.

owner_agent_id.description:
The owning agent, or null for the user. Archiving an agent
clears it and leaves the record usable.

decision.description:
`approved` or `denied`. A form submission is `approved` with
`values`; a dismissal is `denied`.

scope.description:
`once` (the default), or `always` to also write the request's
proposed allow rules into the agent's grant.
Meaningful for a `tool_action` only.

values.description:
What a `form` or a `choice` submits, validated against the
field schema on the row.

DeleteMailboxRequest.description:
The address, typed back. A delete takes the host's mail with it, so
the user says which mailbox in full.

DeletedMailboxDto.description:
What the delete did. `notice` carries the words a manual host asks
the desk to show, because that mailbox is still at the host.

DeltaFrame.description:
One `message.delta` WS payload. `catch_up: true` carries the whole
accumulated text; a live frame carries one delta. A client applies a
frame only when `seq` follows the last one it folded.

agent_id.description:
The agent writing the message; the client names the row with it
before the durable row arrives.

parent_message_id.description: Set when the streaming message is a thread reply.

seq.description: The count of deltas folded into this frame's text end position.

DictateClientFrame.description:
Frames the browser sends on the dictation socket. The session cookie
authenticated the upgrade, so the socket carries no
credential: PCM16 audio goes as binary frames, and `commit` is the
release.

DictateServerFrame.description:
Frames the daemon sends on the dictation socket. `ready` says whether
text arrives live; the socket ends after `transcript.final` or
`error`.

DockerCandidateDto.description: One candidate endpoint and what it answered.

error.description: Why the candidate did not answer, when it did not.

DockerReportDto.description: Docker discovery as the System tab shows it.

endpoint.description:
The endpoint in use: the first candidate that answered. Null
means Pagis found no Docker, and agent computers do not run.

DropTierRequest.description:
The user drops the tier of a live call. `unknown` is the only value:
a tier rises by itself and falls by hand (ADR-0021).

public_origin.description:
The absolute `https://` or `http://` origin that the owner's proxy
or tunnel answers on, such as `https://pagis.example.net`. Its host
is not loopback.

trusted_proxy.description:
The IP address the proxy or tunnel reaches the daemon from:
`127.0.0.1` for one on this machine. Null or empty believes no
forwarded header.

EventRow.description: An `events` row as sent on the firehose, verbatim.

FailureKind.description: The cause recorded where a Run fails. The error holds the detail.

FilterPreview.description:
What one filter decides about the stored pages of a resource, for
the filter editor. The counts come from Page Signals alone.

rules.description: Per rule, in filter order: the pages that rule decides first.

FormField.description:
One flat form field. There is no nesting, no conditional
visibility, and no layout hint.

key.description: The key the submitted value lands under.

options.description: The choices of a `select` field; empty for every other kind.

agent_name.description: Denormalized so the settings page renders standalone.

allow.description:
The allow rules — command prefixes on a host grant, registrable
domains on a credential grant. Empty is per-action mode.

capabilities.description: Named capabilities on a Connection grant.

resource_id.description:
What the grant reaches: the Connection, the Plugin, or the machine
of a host grant. A credential grant names none.

HealthDto.description:
What the desktop shell reads before it attaches to a daemon it did
not start (ADR-0025): the daemon answers, and it says its version.

HostDto.description: One machine of one Person, with whether it is connected now.

capabilities.description: What the client declared it can do, for example `shell`.

platform.description: The operating system family the client reported.

present.description:
True while the daemon holds this machine's connection. A host
action runs only on a present machine.

IceServerDto.description: One ICE server the browser configures before it offers.

InstallationHealthDto.description: The health of the daemon, as an Administrator reads it.

container_quota.description:
Whether this machine holds the writable container layer of a
Computer to its size: `supported`, `unsupported`, or `unknown`
until a Computer wakes after the daemon starts or when the limits
name no layer size. `unsupported` means that nothing bounds what
an Agent writes outside `/data` while its Computer is awake, which
https://docs.pagis.co/server/computers#bound-a-computers-disk says how to fix.

docker_endpoint.description:
The Docker endpoint in use, or `null` where Pagis found none and
no Computer runs.

queued_runs.description: The Runs waiting to start, over every Workspace.

running_runs.description: The Runs a model is answering now.

unfinished_runs.description:
Every Run of the installation that has not finished, which is
the two counts above and the Runs parked on a person.

volume_quota.description:
Whether this machine holds a Computer volume to its size:
`supported`, `unsupported`, or `unknown` while Docker does not
answer or the limits name no volume size. `unsupported` means
that nothing bounds what `/data` holds, which
https://docs.pagis.co/server/computers#bound-a-computers-disk says how to fix.

KeypadCodeDto.description:
Whether the Workspace holds a Keypad Code, and the wrong codes its
callers entered. It is everything the API says about the code: there
is no reveal and no export.

failed_attempts.description:
The wrong codes on every Call and every line of the Workspace,
since a correct code or the person last cleared the count.

suspended_until.description:
The end of the latest delay, in Unix milliseconds. `null` until
the first delay starts. It stays when the delay ends, until the
count is cleared.

oneOf.description: Prose. An agent's own text becomes markdown blocks.
A declarative grid: no server pagination, no sort configuration.

The view of a `form` Request: fill then submit. Live state and
the submitted values come from the Request row.
The view of a `choice` Request: one tap.

The view of a `tool_action` Request. Daemon-minted: an agent
that could mint one would forge authority over its own gate.

Derived run progress. The daemon composes the text; there is no
tool that writes it.
An image artifact, fetched through the daemon.
A non-image artifact, downloaded through the daemon.
A live view of one agent's computer screen.

A call, live or over (ADR-0020). While the call runs, the
block listens to it.

One Widget of a Software Package, rendered in a sandboxed frame
(ADR-0016). It carries no HTML and no data: the UI reads
the page by package, version and Widget name, and the data by
tool call id. `request_id` is set when the Widget asks the user
and the Run parks on the answer.

text.description:
The author's plain-text projection of what the Widget
shows. It is foreign text, so the projection labels it.

oneOf.description:
One mail, inbound or sent (ADR-0019). It carries the
envelope and never the words: the inspector reads the headers
and the text body live through the daemon, which stores none of
them.

counterpart.description:
The other party: who sent an inbound mail, and who a sent
mail went to. Foreign text on an inbound mail.

mailbox.description:
The mailbox the message reached: the Agent's own address,
or the alias of one of the user's accounts. It labels the
line, and the inspector reads the message through it.

subject.description: The subject. Foreign text on an inbound mail.

oneOf.description:
The tier of the sender, stamped before the Agent read a
word (ADR-0019). A mail the Agent sent carries none.

KnownBlock.description: The block types the daemon and the UI both know.

agent_id.description:
The Agent whose list this row joins, or absent for the
Workspace-wide list.

value.description:
An E.164 number, an email address or a bare domain. The daemon
reads which of the three it is.

ListedModelDto.description: One model a provider lists, in candidate form.

context_window.description:
The context window, after the layers: the provider's report,
then the built-in table, then the conservative default.

input_cost.description:
USD per million input tokens, or `null` when no layer prices the
model: its cost is unknown, never zero.

output_cost.description: USD per million output tokens, or `null` when unknown.

oneOf.description: `PCMU` or `PCMA`: the law of every binary frame that follows.
The call ended, with the reason it ended for.

ListenServerFrame.description:
Frames the daemon sends beside the audio. `ready` names the codec
of the frames that follow; the socket ends after `ended` or
`error`.

MailAttachmentDto.description: One attachment: the name and the size, never the bytes (ADR-0019).

MailDirection.description: Which way one mail went (ADR-0019): into the mailbox, or out of it.

MailHeaderDto.description: One header of a message, in the order the message carries them.

MailMessageDto.description:
One message as the inspector shows it. It is read live and stored
nowhere.

mailbox.description: The mailbox it was read from, as the block names it.

text.description: The text body. HTML became text at the transport.

MailboxDto.description:
One Agent Mailbox as the desk shows it. The password is never part
of it (ADR-0013).

address.description: The address itself. It never changes.

allow_rules.description:
The Mail Recipient Domain allow rules the user wrote from a
send card (ADR-0019). A send whose recipients all sit on these
registrable domains needs no card.

connection_id.description: The Mailbox Provider Connection that carries it.

outgoing_cap.description: The most messages a day this mailbox may send.

reason.description: Why the mailbox is `unavailable`, in the words the user reads.

sends_today.description: How many it has sent today.

MailboxListPage.description:
Every mailbox of the Workspace that is not a tombstone. The
Connections page reads it to say which mailboxes sit on a Mailbox
Provider, and which Agent holds each one (ADR-0019).

MailboxNameDto.description:
What the form says under the name field as the user types
(ADR-0019). It is a read: it reserves nothing, and the Address
Ledger stays the one place that refuses a taken address.

address.description: The whole address the name makes on that provider's domain.

available.description: Whether the address is free and the name is allowed.

reason.description: Why it is not, in the words the user reads.

MailboxOfferDto.description:
One Mailbox Provider the form can offer, and the name this Agent
would take on it (ADR-0019).

default_outgoing_cap.description:
The messages a day a new mailbox gets unless the user says
otherwise.

deletes_mailbox.description:
Whether the host deletes the mailbox. Where it does not, the
user deletes it at the host afterwards.

mints_password.description:
Whether the host mints the mailbox password. Where it does not,
the user types the password of an inbox made at the host.

suggested_local_part.description:
The local part the form fills in, with the ledger collision
suffix on it when the plain name is taken. Empty when the
Agent's name carries nothing an address can hold.

MailboxPage.description:
The Agent's mailbox, and what it could have instead when it has
none. One read serves the creation form and the mailbox card.

offers.description: The Mailbox Providers that are `connected` now.

MailboxProviderDto.description:
What one Mailbox Provider holds and what it can do
(ADR-0019). A capability that is absent is shown as absent, so the
page says what the user must do by hand.

delete_mailbox.description:
The host deletes the mailbox. Without it the user deletes the
mailbox at the host.

domain.description: The domain the mailboxes live on, e.g. `example.com`.

idle.description: The transport waits for new mail instead of polling.

outgoing_cap.description:
The host caps the mailbox's own sends. The daemon enforces the
Outgoing Cap for every host either way.

reset_password.description:
The daemon mints a new mailbox password. Without it the user
pastes one.

MediaRelayKind.description:
Which Media Relay carries the live screen (ADR-0014): `daemon`
forwards media in the daemon, and `turn` puts an external TURN server
in front of the browser leg.

MemoryCommitDiffDto.description: The change one commit made, per file.

MemoryFeedAction.description: One action the learning feed can apply without another model turn.

MemoryFeedItem.description: One learning feed entry: a Reflection commit, a revert, or a wake-only Schedule.

agent_id.description:
The Agent that wrote the entry. A revert has no author Agent; it
names the owner of the private files it touched, if any.

agent_name.description:
Denormalized so the feed renders standalone; `None` for
user-side entries (reverts, the onboarding seed).

id.description: The event ULID; the page cursor.

message_id.description:
The reply the Run settled; the Thread shows the learned line
under it.

reverted_sha.description: For `reverted`: the commit the inverse commit undoes.

sha.description: The commit this entry is about. Empty for a Schedule entry.

source_kind.description:
Where the change came from: `thread` (a conversation Run),
`sync` (an arrival Run), `backfill` (a historical arrival Run),
or `revert`. `None` for a Schedule entry and for a commit with
no Run, such as the onboarding seed.

titles.description:
The name a person reads for each of `files`, in the same order:
the page title, never a path or an id.

MemoryFileDto.description: A fact file. The desk reads it and does not edit it.

kind.description:
One of the page kinds (ADR-0007), or another word the page
declares. A word outside the vocabulary is kept as it is.

sources.description:
The sources of a Subject Page's Timeline, most entries first.
Empty for a page without a Timeline.

title.description: The title from the front matter or the first heading.

MemoryHunkDto.description:
One changed range of one file: the lines before and the lines
after, each with its one-based first line number. A range with no
lines on one side starts at the line the other side replaces.

MemoryPageAuthorDto.description: The pages one author changed last.

agent_id.description: The agent of the author. `None` for the user and for Pagis.

MemoryPageCountsDto.description: How many pages a scope holds.

MemoryPageDto.description: One file of a scope, as the Memory page lists it.

changed_at.description: The time of the last commit that changed the file.

changed_by.description: The commit author's name: an agent, `User`, or `Pagis`.

kind.description:
One of the page kinds (ADR-0007), or another word the page
declares. A word outside the vocabulary is kept as it is.

source_connection_id.description:
The connection that wrote most of the page's Timeline. `None`
for a page written from conversations.

next.description: The `after` of the next part. `None` at the end of the list.

total.description: How many pages match the query, in all parts.

MemoryPageSourceDto.description: One source that wrote Timeline entries of a page.

connection_id.description:
The connection the entries came through; `None` for a
reference that names no connection.

blocks.description:
The typed block array (ADR-0004). A block type this daemon does
not know is served unchanged and renders as the UI fallback, so
the union is open at both ends.

pending_id.description: The client-generated send dedup key; present on user sends.

ModelCheckDto.description:
What one key check proved: the provider listed its models for the
key.

available.description: How many models the provider lists for the key.

ModelListsDto.description: The lists of every provider that holds a key.

MultiUserDto.description: The multi-user mode as the Settings view shows it (ADR-0024).

enabled.description:
Whether the installation serves People on other machines: its
Public Origin host is not loopback.

public_origin.description: The Public Origin people open. Null when the mode is off.

switchable.description:
Whether an Administrator can switch the mode here. Only a local
installation can: a server always serves a network, and its
deployment names the Public Origin.

trusted_proxy.description: The address whose forwarded headers the daemon believes, or null.

MyUsageDto.description: What the signed-in person spent, and the cap they are under.

monthly_spend_cap_usd.description: The person's monthly Spend Cap, or `null` where they have none.

NamedValueDto.description:
One `env` entry or one header, as the package writes it. The value
is shown whole: it is package data, and a reference to a bound
field is what the user must be able to read (ADR-0017).

NewMailboxRequest.description:
The mailbox section of the Agent creation form, and the body of a
later provision (ADR-0019).

connection_id.description: The Mailbox Provider Connection to make it on.

local_part.description: The name before the `@`, on that Connection's domain.

outgoing_cap.description: The messages a day; absent takes the default.

password.description:
The password of an inbox the user made at a manual host. A host
with an API mints its own and refuses this.

OnboardingDto.description: Everything the onboarding wizard needs in one read.

docker.description:
Docker discovery. A Member reads the endpoint in use and no
candidate: the candidates name the sockets of the installation's
own host.

docker_endpoint.description:
The Docker endpoint an Administrator typed, or `null` for
discovery. It is `null` for a Member.

oneOf.description:
The current server-owned key check. `null` when no check passed,
or when the checked credential has changed since.

OwnAddressDto.description:
One address that is owner because the user holds the account it
belongs to (ADR-0019). It is not a row, so it has no id and the user
cannot remove it.

connection_alias.description: The Connection this address is the account of.

client_name.description:
The machine name a Client App sends, which makes the Session a
Client App Session with that name. A browser sends none.

timezone.description:
The IANA timezone of the browser or the Client App. At the
Person's first sign-in it becomes their timezone, so their
Schedules run on their clock and not on the server's.

PersonDto.description: One Person on the roster, with what an Administrator manages.

last_signed_in_at.description: When a client last signed in as this Person.

monthly_spend_cap_usd.description: The monthly Spend Cap in US dollars, or `null` for no cap.

workspace_id.description:
The Workspace this Person owns, or `null` where the seed has not
written one. The usage read names the Workspace, so the roster
carries it.

PersonResourcesDto.description: What one Person's Computers take of the host.

awake_computers.description: How many Computers of this Person are awake now.

containers.description: The tenant's containers, awake or not.

volume_bytes.description:
The bytes those volumes take, or `null` where Docker did not
answer: a missing figure is not a failed page.

volumes.description: The named volumes of the tenant's Agents.

PersonUsageDto.description: What one Person spent over the period, for the Administrator's read.

cap_reached.description:
True when the period is the current month and the total has
reached the person's cap, so the roster says who is stopped.

PhoneNumberDto.description:
One number the Workspace owns. `provider_number_id` is not here and
never will be: it is the carrier's handle, not the user's.

agent_id.description: The Agent that holds the line, when one does.

connection_id.description: The carrier Connection that carries the number.

registration.description:
Where the line of the number's carrier stands with the
registrar: `unregistered`, `registering`, `registered` or
`failed`. One line carries every number of the carrier. Absent
when no Agent holds the number, because a call to it is refused
whatever the line does. An unregistered line drops inbound calls
in silence, so the Agent's page shows this.

PhoneNumberPage.description:
The numbers of the Workspace, and the carrier they came from. The
carrier's status decides whether Settings shows the search or a
reconnect action in its place.

PluginBindingDto.description: What one field is bound to. A secret binding carries no value.

changed.description: What an update changed. It is empty for every other answer.

frozen_tools.description:
The frozen manifest of the installed state. It is empty until
the Plugin is enabled and its servers have been read once.

tools_changed.description:
Whether a server has offered a different tool list than the
frozen one. An update accepts the difference (ADR-0017).

PluginDto.description:
One Plugin in full: the record, what it declares, and what it is
bound to. It is the install card.

PluginFieldDto.description: One config field the Plugin declares.

PluginFrozenToolDto.description:
One tool of the frozen manifest (ADR-0017): what a server
offered at install, and what the model calls it.

server.description: The `mcp.json` name of the server that offers it.

PluginLogDto.description: The end of one Plugin's server log in the asking Person's Workspace.

PluginRowDto.description: One row of the Plugins list.

PluginServerDto.description: One MCP server the Plugin declares.

running.description:
Whether the server holds a process now. A server starts
at the first call and stops when it is idle, so a stopped
server is the usual state and not a fault.

PluginSkillDto.description:
One Skill the Plugin ships (ADR-0017). The plugin page shows
the list read-only: a Skill is the Plugin's, and only an update
changes it.

ref.description: The branch, tag or commit. Absent takes the default branch.

artifact_id.description: The Artifact that holds the plugin directory as one tar.

PluginSourceRequest.description:
Where the files of a Plugin come from. An upload arrives as an
Artifact: the desk uploads the tar of the directory first and names
it here.

PluginToolEffectDto.description:
The effect class one tool takes at dispatch: what the Plugin
declared, or `host` for every tool it did not (ADR-0017).

PointerDto.description:
A derived DM pointer entry: this DM's agent posted in
another channel. Computed at query time from that message; `id` is
the source message's id, so the page cursor stays uniform.

channel_id.description: The channel the agent posted in.

id.description: The source message's id — also this item's cursor position.

preview.description: The source message's text, for the pointer's preview line.

ProgressFrame.description:
One `progress.state` WS payload: the whole current text, never a
delta. A client applies a frame only when `seq` is newer than the
one it holds, so a catch-up never loses to a stale live frame.

agent_id.description: The agent working; the client names a synthetic row with it.

parent_message_id.description: Set when the run is bound to a thread.

ProviderEntryDto.description:
One provider Pagis connects, as the picker draws it. The
client holds no provider list of its own.

absent_capabilities.description:
What this provider does not do, and a sibling provider does:
a carrier that carries no text lists `texting` here (ADR-0020).

blurb.description: What the user reads before they type.

browser_sign_in.description:
True for the `oauth` entry of a brokered flow in which the browser
that goes to the provider can first ask the Person to sign in to
Pagis. False on a local installation with the multi-user mode
off, whose start route asks for no Session, and for every other
entry.

capabilities.description:
What a Connection of this provider gives an Agent: `mail`,
`calendar`, `mailboxes`, `telephony` or `texting`.

kind.description:
`oauth` when the user finishes at the provider in the browser,
`fields` when the form below is the whole setup.

max_instances.description:
How many Connections of this provider one Workspace holds, or
null for as many as the user makes.

portal.description: Where the user finds the values, e.g. `the Telnyx portal`.

ProviderFieldDto.description: One value a provider's setup form asks for.

hint.description: The placeholder, with an example value.

key.description: The key the create request carries the value under.

secret.description:
The form masks it, and the daemon never writes it to the
database.

ProviderKeyDto.description:
One provider's key status. `source` is `env`, `config`, or
`secret_file` when a key is configured.

ProviderModelsDto.description: One provider's list, or why it is missing.

error.description: The provider's own words when the list call failed.

models.description:
Newest first where the provider reports a release order. Empty
when `error` is set.

preselected.description:
The model id a default pick takes: the newest listed model whose
name reads as a chat model. `None` when the list has none.

ProviderSetupDto.description: One provider as the installation sets it up.

provider.description: The catalog id or the model provider id.

ReplyAuthorDto.description: One author of the replies in a thread.

ReportDto.description:
The Report that Home reads (ADR-0022): the newest message the Report
Schedule wrote, and the state of the Report that runs now.

oneOf.description: The newest written Report; `null` before the first one.

next_due_at.description: When the next Report is due.

schedule_id.description: The Schedule behind the Report; `null` when the Workspace has none.

writing_run_id.description: The Run writing a Report now; `null` when none writes.

payload.description:
The trusted content the daemon minted the row with: tool name
and arguments for an action, the field schema for a form, the
options for a choice.

state.description:
`pending`, `approved`, `denied`, `expired`, or `superseded`
(the user sent a message in place of a decision).

values.description: What a form or a choice submitted with its decision.

ResetMailboxPasswordRequest.description: The new password, when the host does not mint one itself.

awake_on_server.description:
How many Computers the whole server holds awake now, and how
many it may.

RestartDto.description: The daemon's answer to a restart request.

exit_code.description:
The code the daemon exits with. The shell starts it again on
this code.

RetentionPolicyDto.description:
One class's retention window. `retain_days` of `null` keeps the
class for ever, which is the default (ADR-0020).

Rule.description: One rule: a verdict and the conditions that must all hold for it.

outcome.description: `canceling`, or `already_ended` when the run was terminal.

hop_count.description: The count of agent-to-agent hops behind this run.

origin_channel_id.description:
The channel the delegation chain owes its answer to.
The Desk Panel reads it to know which Agent works on a
Delegation the Chief of Staff started (ADR-0022).

RunSpendDto.description:
One Run's spend, for the person's own Usage page. The Run
transcript has a usage shape of its own (`runs::RunUsageDto`), which
reports the tokens of one Run and no money.

ended_at.description: Null while the step is live.

index.description: The step's position in the Run, from 1.

live.description: True on the step the Run works on now.

screenshot_id.description:
The Artifact of the screenshot taken during the step, when there
is one.

RunStepKind.description: The tool family a step used.

failure.description: The reason line of a failed Run.

oneOf.description: Present on a stopped Run.

worked_ms.description: The time from the Run's start to its end, or null while it works.

after_ms.description: The time the Run worked before the stop.

ScreenDto.description:
The Media Relay of the running daemon as the Settings view shows
it (ADR-0014). The live screen does not go through the proxy or
tunnel of the multi-user mode, so the view names where it goes.

advertise_ip.description: `[screen] advertise_ip`: the address the relay gives to browsers.

loopback.description:
Whether `advertise_ip` is loopback. Then only this machine
reaches the `daemon` relay.

media_port_first.description: The first UDP port of the relay's range.

media_port_last.description: The last UDP port of the relay's range.

ScreenIceBody.description: What a browser needs before it opens a screen session.

ice_servers.description:
Empty when the browser reaches the Media Relay by itself, which
is what a local installation and the `daemon` relay do.

SdpBody.description:
One WebRTC SDP payload: the browser's offer up, screend's
answer back.

artifact_ids.description:
Pre-uploaded attachments, rendered as `image`/`file`
blocks after the text.

parent_message_id.description: Reply target; must be a top-level message in the same channel.

pending_id.description:
Client-generated dedup key; resending the same value in the same
channel returns the original message instead of a duplicate.

ServerFrame.description:
The server envelope. Domain events carry `seq` (the event id) and an
`EventRow` payload; control frames (`ready`, `pong`, `resync`,
`error`) carry no `seq` and are never replayed.

replay.description: True for a domain event replayed after reconnect.

SessionDto.description: One live Session, for the read that says who is signed in.

client_name.description: The machine name of a Client App Session, or null.

current.description:
True for the Session the reading Administrator holds, so the
list never reads as somebody else's client.

SetAnalyticsRequest.description: Turn the anonymous analytics on or off.

code.description: 6 to 8 digits. It is hashed at once and never read back.

model.description:
The model id as the provider lists it, without the provider
prefix. `null` takes the preselection: the newest listed chat model,
or the provider's fallback candidate when its list is not available.

docker_endpoint.description:
A socket path, a `unix://` or a `tcp://` endpoint. Null gives
discovery the choice back. Pagis pings the endpoint before it
saves.

retain_days.description: Whole days to keep the class, or `null` to keep it for ever.

monthly_spend_cap_usd.description: The monthly cap in US dollars, or `null` to take the cap away.

SetupFactDto.description:
One value a part states about what the installation holds, or what
the administrator copies into the provider's console. It is never a
secret.

SetupPartDto.description:
One part of a provider that the installation sets up, and where it
stands.

blurb.description: What the administrator reads before they type.

connection_id.description: The Installation Connection this part is, once it exists.

fields.description:
What the form asks for. A secret field is masked and never read
back.

id.description: The path segment the routes name the part by.

status.description:
The Connection's status, for a Connection part that exists:
`connected`, `unavailable` or `reauth_required`.

testable.description: Whether a test proves the kept credential at the provider.

SetupStateDto.description: What the first-run flow still needs.

administration_origin.description:
The origin of the Administration Port, where the first
Administrator is made. It binds loopback by default, so a person
on another machine reaches it through an SSH tunnel.

configured_providers.description:
Which of them already hold a key, from the environment, the
config file or the secret store.

providers.description: The provider ids the flow may take a key for.

Signal.description: One fact the filter editor offers for one resource.

contributions.description: Every Contribution offered to this package, newest first.

origin_package.description: The package this one was forked from, when it is a Fork.

SoftwarePackageDto.description: One row of the Software List.

author_name.description: The Agent that wrote the package, by name.

open_contributions.description: How many Contributions to this package are still open.

tool_count.description: How many tools the latest Version carries.

SoftwareToolDto.description: One tool of the latest Version.

SoftwareVersionDto.description: One published Version. The files stay in the repository.

SourceBatchDto.description: One collection pass, as the collector health card reads it.

detail.description: A stable failure code, never provider text.

oneOf.description: The most recent collection pass on this source.
The newest Incoming Event this rule matched.
The most recent pass that did not fail.

SubscriptionDetailDto.description: The subscription with everything a detail view needs beside it.

blocked_reason.description: Why a blocked rule is blocked.

source_version.description: The Capability Manifest version the rule pins.

filter.description: The rules that decide which Subject Pages reflect (ADR-0011).

required_capability.description: The adapter's read capability, set by the daemon, never the model.

arrival_skipped.description: Arrivals that a permanent rejection or five attempts stopped.

backfill_capped.description: True while the budget of the backfill window is spent.

backfill_failed.description: Backfill pages whose Runs failed at the attempt limit (ADR-0011).

backfill_pending.description: Backfill pages that reflect and wait for a Run (ADR-0011).

backfill_reflected.description: Backfill pages that a Run already reflects.

filter_revision.description: The revision of the Reflection Filter these counts belong to.

incomplete_versions.description: Upsert versions that hold no metadata yet (ADR-0011).

reflected_pages.description: Pages the current filter revision sent to reflection.

skipped_pages.description: Pages the current filter revision held back.

SystemSettingsDto.description: Every System Setting in one read.

data_directory.description: Read-only: where the daemon keeps its data.

docker_endpoint.description: The Docker endpoint the user typed, or null for discovery.

listening_port.description: The product port the daemon listens on.

port_override.description:
What sets `listening_port` over the file for this run: `--port`
or `PAGIS_PORT`. Null when the file sets it. A port that differs
with no override is a change that the next start puts in effect.

screen.description:
The Media Relay the running daemon serves the live screen
through. A change to `[screen]` takes effect at the next start.

started_at.description:
When this daemon process started, in Unix milliseconds. A
restart changes it.

supervised.description:
Whether a supervisor (the Client App, or the restart policy of
the compose deployment) starts the daemon again after it exits
for a restart. Without one, a person runs `pagis` again.

version.description:
The running daemon's version. The Client App reads it to know
whether it may attach to a daemon it did not start.

TableCell.description: One table cell: a closed union, so a cell carries no markup.

key.description: The column's stable key; the UI sorts on it.

ThreadDto.description: One thread: the root message plus its replies, oldest first.

TimelineItem.description: One timeline entry: a message, or a derived DM pointer.

blocks.description:
The typed block array (ADR-0004). A block type this daemon does
not know is served unchanged and renders as the UI fallback, so
the union is open at both ends.

pending_id.description: The client-generated send dedup key; present on user sends.

reply_authors.description:
The different authors of the replies, the newest reply first,
at most three.

reply_count.description: The count of replies in this message's thread.

TimelineMessageDto.description:
A top-level message with its thread rollup, computed in the
timeline query.

TranscriptLineDto.description: One line of a Call transcript, as the UI reads it.

TrustEntryDto.description: One Trust List entry. A row with no `agent_id` is Workspace-wide.

value.description: The E.164 number, the bare address or the bare domain.

own_addresses.description: The addresses that are owner with no row.

TrustTier.description:
What the words of one Remote Party are worth (ADR-0021). The tier
gates authority and never access: Pagis answers a call from any
number, and the tier decides whose words can move the Agent.

The order is the authority order, so `min` is the rule of ADR-0021:
a tier is the smaller of the tier caller ID proposes and the tier
the Keypad Code proves.

artifact_id.description:
The new upload, for a Plugin that was uploaded. A Plugin
installed from a repository reads that repository again.

root_message_id.description:
The Thread root. Absent keeps the Thread while the Channel stays
the same, and drops it when the Channel changes. `null` clears
the Thread.

The Thread root. Absent keeps the Thread while the Channel stays
the same, and drops it when the Channel changes. `null` clears
the Thread.

docker_endpoint.description:
A socket path, a `unix://` or a `tcp://` endpoint. Null clears
the override and gives discovery the choice back. Pagis pings
the endpoint before it saves.

UploadForm.description: The multipart upload shape: one `file` part with the bytes.

calls.description: How many model calls the total holds.

cost_usd.description: The sum of the known costs.

unpriced_calls.description:
How many of those calls ran on a model with no known price, whose
cost `cost_usd` does not hold.

UserDto.description: What the shell knows about the person it serves.

oneOf.description:
Where the Administration Interface answers, for an Administrator.
The product links to it and draws no installation setting of its
own. `null` for a Member.

email.description:
The address the person signs in with; `null` for the seeded
person of a local installation.

name.description:
The name the agents call the person by; `null` until onboarding
records one.

ValueKind.description:
What a signal or a condition value holds.

`Duration` and `List` are value kinds of a condition, not signal
kinds: a duration applies to a DateTime signal, and a list applies to
a text signal. A `List` signal is a text signal that also tells the
editor which form its values have.

VoicePage.description: The voice catalogue (ADR-0020): the names an Agent Voice can take.

channel_id.description: The destination for a conversation Run. An arrival has no Channel.

rule_id.description: The rule this Wake-up delivers for.

source_count.description: How many source occurrences this Wake-up combines.

WidgetViewDto.description:
The half of a Widget view that is data: what the tool was called
with, and what it answered. The host pushes them into the view as
`ui/notifications/tool-input` and `ui/notifications/tool-result`.

WorkspaceDto.description: The Workspace the shell reads once at start.

chief_of_staff_agent_id.description: The Chief of Staff; `null` when no Agent is active.

report_schedule_id.description: The Schedule that writes the Report for Home (ADR-0022).

timezone.description: The IANA timezone new wall-clock schedules copy.
